decisions.name: Levi decomposition and semisimple structure
decisions.reason: The selected plan places Levi and semisimple structure on the next page after the radical and nilradical suppliers constructed here.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: The current plan places solvable-and-nilpotent-lie-algebras at 497 and its consumer semisimple-lie-algebras-cohomology-and-levi-theory at 499. The latter current draft explicitly contains thm-semisimple-lie-algebras-decompose-as-direct-sums-of-simple-ideals, thm-levi-decomposition and thm-malcev-conjugacy-of-levi-subalgebras. Kirillov structure/Levi development is therefore supplied at the named destination after the radical definitions, rather than dropped.

decisions.name: Hausdorff-series integration of nilpotent Lie algebras
decisions.reason: Global integration and the nilpotent exponential diffeomorphism belong to the following Levi-and-integration page, not this algebraic structure page.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Milne I §2 Hausdorff-series discussion and the later nilpotent integration treatment distinguish algebraic nilpotence from the group law. The named destination at order 499 has the Lie-group/covering closure and explicitly contains thm-the-exponential-map-of-a-connected-simply-connected-nilpotent-lie-group-is-a-diffeomorphism and cor-connected-nilpotent-lie-groups-are-discrete-central-quotients-of-bch-groups. The algebraic source page at 497 does not need that later group result. Deferral stands.

decisions.name: root systems and classification of split semisimple algebras
decisions.reason: Root decomposition and Dynkin classification are not required by either selected pair and would create a substantial unused inventory beyond the current plan.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Milne Table of Contents separates Chapter I §§7–9 root systems, split semisimple classification and their representations from §§4–6 structure, Weyl, Levi and Ado. Current semisimple page follows invariant forms, Casimir cohomology and Levi/Ado/integration, without consuming a root-classification theorem. Root/Dynkin classification would add a substantial distinct development. Exclusion stands.

decisions.name: Cartan's trace criterion for solvability
decisions.reason: The criterion is intentionally supplied on the immediately following semisimple page, where trace forms and the Killing form have first been defined.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Milne Chapter I §3/§4 places the trace criterion at the solvable/semisimple boundary. Current thm-cartans-solvability-criterion is explicitly homed on the named order-499 destination after def-trace-form-of-a-finite-dimensional-representation and def-killing-form-of-a-finite-dimensional-lie-algebra. The preceding order-497 page proves its radical/nilradical chain using Lie/Engel, not a forward Cartan citation. Deferral stands.

decisions.name: Cartan criteria and semisimple structure theory
decisions.reason: These results are consumers of the radical and nilradical theory and are assigned to the next selected A page.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Knapp Chapter I Cartan/semisimple development belongs after the solvable/nilpotent structure. The current named destination contains thm-cartans-solvability-criterion, thm-cartans-semisimplicity-criterion and the simple-ideal decomposition, with trace/Killing definitions before them. The source page supplies radical and nilradical prerequisites at order 497; the destination is order 499. This is an implemented in-run deferral, not a missing claim.

decisions.name: Lie algebra homology and the enveloping-algebra Tor interpretation
decisions.reason: The assigned page needs cohomology and its extension applications, while Lie homology and derived-functor calculations have no consumer in either selected pair.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Weibel §7.2 Definition 7.2.2 and Examples 7.2.3 distinguish homology as derived coinvariants/Tor from cohomology as derived invariants/Ext. Current Chevalley–Eilenberg cochains, differential, Whitehead and abelian-extension items develop cohomology directly and do not invoke a Tor computation. The distinct homological package has no consumer in either Lie pair; exclusion stands.

decisions.name: Engel's theorem statement without its proof
decisions.reason: This treatment explicitly omits the proof, so it was not used as proof evidence; the complete Milne and Knapp arguments supply that role.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Kirillov introduction explicitly says Engel and PBW proofs are omitted; this is visible in the complete source text, not inferred from a failed search. Current lem-engel-common-zero-vector, thm-engels-triangularization-theorem and thm-engels-theorem are retained on the source page with independent Milne/Knapp backing. Declining this source as proof evidence does not decline Engel itself, so the decision stands.

decisions.name: root decompositions and classification examples
decisions.reason: Those later chapters begin the root-system and classification track, which is neither a prerequisite nor a consumer requirement of this batch.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Kirillov Chapter 7 explicitly separates root decomposition, Dynkin diagrams, Serre relations and classification; Chapter 8 develops highest-weight representations. The current semisimple page proves its invariant-form, Whitehead, Levi and integration contracts without invoking those classification results. They are a distinct downstream track rather than a missing local dependency, so exclusion stands.
